questions.enonce_markdown:
CAL is a pedagogic approach gradually being used in Cameroon today.

(a) Define Computer Assisted Learning (CAL) (1 mark)

(b) Briefly discuss TWO course delivery methods used in CAL. (2 marks)

(c) Explain ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of CAL in Cameroon. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) CAL (1 mark).** Computer Assisted Learning (or Computer Aided Learning) is the use of computers and educational software (tutorials, simulations, drill-and-practice programs, multimedia lessons, quizzes) to deliver, support and test learning, so that the learner can learn with the computer, often at his or her own pace.

**(b) Two course delivery methods (2 marks, 1 mark each).** Any two:

- **Stand-alone delivery on CD-ROM, DVD or a flash disk:** the courseware is installed on the learner's computer, and no network is needed; it suits places with no internet, but the content is not updated easily.
- **Local network or intranet delivery:** the lessons are stored on a server in the school or university and the learners reach them from computers in a computer laboratory.
- **Internet or web-based delivery (e-learning):** the course is put on a learning management system (for example Moodle) or a website, and is reached from anywhere through a browser, with e-mail, forums and video lessons; learning can be synchronous (live class) or asynchronous (at any time).
- **Blended learning:** classroom teaching combined with computer-based activities.

**(c) One advantage and one disadvantage in Cameroon (2 marks).**

- *Advantage:* the learner works at his or her own pace and can repeat a lesson as often as needed; pupils in remote areas or in overcrowded classes can reach good lessons and many resources (and the lessons use sound, images and simulations that make difficult topics such as science easier to understand).
- *Disadvantage:* the cost of computers and software, together with the unreliable electricity supply and the expensive and slow internet connection, means that many schools, especially in rural areas, cannot use it; there is also a lack of teachers trained to use and prepare computer-based lessons.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following Database terms:

(a) Relationship. (1 mark)

(b) Attribute. (1 mark)

(c) Entity. (1 mark)

(d) Redundancy. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Relationship (1 mark).** A relationship is an association or link between two entities (tables) of a database, for example "a teacher teaches many students". It is of one-to-one, one-to-many or many-to-many type, and in a relational database it is implemented by a foreign key in one table that refers to the primary key of the other table.

**(b) Attribute (1 mark).** An attribute is a property or characteristic that describes an entity: it is stored as a field (a column) of the table, for example the attributes *Name*, *Date of birth* and *Class* of the entity STUDENT.

**(c) Entity (1 mark).** An entity is a person, place, object, event or concept about which data is stored in the database (for example a student, a teacher, a book); an entity type is represented by a table and each occurrence of it by a record (a row).

**(d) Redundancy (1 mark).** Redundancy is the unnecessary repetition of the same data in several places (several records or tables) of a database. It wastes storage and leads to inconsistency and update, insertion and deletion anomalies; it is reduced by normalisation.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is Normalization in relation to database modeling? (2 marks)

(b) When is a table in a database said to be in First Normal Form? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Normalisation (2 marks).** Normalisation is the process of organising the data of a relational database into well-structured tables, by applying a set of rules called normal forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF...), so that data redundancy is removed and anomalies (insertion, update and deletion anomalies) are avoided. Large tables are split into smaller, related tables that are linked by keys, so that each fact is stored in only one place and data integrity is improved.

**(b) First Normal Form (2 marks).** A table is in First Normal Form (1NF) when:

- every field contains only **atomic (single, indivisible) values**: there are no multivalued attributes and no repeating groups of columns in a record (for example no cell with several telephone numbers);
- each record is unique and the table has a **primary key**; all the values in one column are of the same kind.

For example, a table STUDENT(StudentID, Name, Subjects) with "Maths, Physics" in the field Subjects is not in 1NF; it is converted into 1NF by putting one subject per row (or in a separate table).

questions.enonce_markdown:
In time-sharing multi-programming environment, many users share the same system simultaneously. This situation can result to various security problems.

(a) Identify TWO of such security problems. (2 marks)

(b) Differentiate between multitasking and multiprogramming. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Two security problems (2 marks, 1 mark each).** Any two:

- **Unauthorised access to the files and data of other users:** a user may read, copy, change or delete the data and programs of another user (or of the system) if file permissions and passwords are weak.
- **Interference between programs in memory:** one user's program may read or overwrite the memory area of another program or of the operating system if memory protection fails.
- **Password theft and impersonation** (a user who logs in with another person's account), and loss of privacy when data remain in shared memory or on shared disks.
- **Spread of viruses and malware** from one user's programs to the whole shared system.
- **Denial of service:** one user or a program can use up the processor time, memory or disk space and prevent the others from working.

**(b) Multitasking and multiprogramming (2 marks).**

- **Multiprogramming:** several programs (jobs) are kept in main memory at the same time, and the CPU is switched to another program when the running one has to wait for an input/output operation; the aim is to keep the CPU busy and to increase the use of the resources (throughput).
- **Multitasking:** the CPU executes several tasks (processes or threads) apparently at the same time, by **time-slicing**: it switches rapidly between them after a short time slice, even if they are not waiting, so that each task makes progress and the user gets a quick response (for example a user who listens to music, downloads a file and types a document at once). It is an extension of multiprogramming which is aimed at fast interactive response rather than only at CPU utilisation.
